$comment: THE CAGE, AND IT TRAVELS. Every value here is the same on every box, so git tracks it and a clone is guarded on its first session with nothing typed. A port or a machine path in this file would be dirt on every clone but one, which is why neither is here.
$level0: LEVEL ZERO NAMES ITSELF NOWHERE IN THIS FILE, AND THAT IS THE POINT. A plugin folder under .claude/skills is adopted by the folder it stands in: the client finds .claude/skills/level0/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, loads it as level0@skills-dir, and enables it by default. No marketplace, no registration, and no trust dialog. A marketplace declared here reaches the client only on a workspace whose trust a person has already accepted, which a fresh cloud clone never has, so nothing declared here would load there. See spec/design_output/level0.
$permissions: A ROUTINE FIRES INTO A BOX WITH NOBODY BESIDE IT, SO A PROMPT THERE IS A STALL THAT LASTS UNTIL SOMEBODY LOOKS. THIS FILE HOLDS THE LIST, AND THE MODE STANDS ELSEWHERE: the client takes permissions.defaultMode values auto and bypassPermissions from user settings and managed settings alone, so a project file naming either one changes nothing. The setup script writes the mode into ~/.claude/settings.json before the client starts, and spec/design_output/level0 carries that script. What holds here is allow, which names the tools this tree reaches for anyway. THE DOORS DO NOT LIVE HERE: level zero refuses a landing on main and a breach in a write on its own, and no permission mode reaches those. A CLOUD BOX READS THIS BLOCK, AND A PROBE SAYS SO: on a clone carrying no trust, a deny rule in this file refuses a command, so the trust gate holds the plugin scan and not this file. See spec/design_output/level0.
$hooks: THE BOOT. The boot word of install.sh hands a desk session's hook input to the start verb, and installs the plugin manifest on a cloud box lacking it as a session starts, for the session after it. The timeout in seconds matches startSpan in src/quack/hook_down.go, the span the start road allows the same install. THE BEAT: a box holding a group beats at each turn's end and ends its hold as the session ends, so a takeover reads the box dead at once. See spec/design_output/level0 and spec/design_output/work.
$thinking: THE RETRO READS THE THINKING, SO THE TRANSCRIPT KEEPS IT. By default the client writes each thinking block empty, with its signature alone, so a retro reader finds no doubt and no dropped plan. This asks for the summaries, and the transcript keeps them. See spec/guidance/retro/signals.
